frameBudget.source: docs/performance-budget.md, production-workload table, "Browser callback/main-thread inspection" column. That column declares < 16.67 ms for BOTH the representative 100-unit replay row and the stress 200-unit replay row, so one ceiling governs every fixture here; no per-fixture ceiling is invented.
frameBudget.measures: Chromium AnimationFrame animation_frame_timing_info.duration_ms, which is the same quantity that column describes: one animation-frame callback plus tactical DOM inspection on the production route.
frameBudget.percentileConvention: nearest-rank, values[ceil(n*p)-1], the convention already used by finalize-svg-pipeline-evidence.mjs
frameBudget.exemptJourneyReason: The idle journey performs no interaction and Chromium emits no AnimationFrame records for it (samples=0 in every observed run). A frame budget cannot be evaluated with no frames, so idle is declared exempt and reports `unevaluated` rather than a verdict it did not measure. A NON-exempt journey that reports zero frames is a FAILURE, not an exemption.
frameBudget.notMeasuredHere: The same table's "Release projection p95" column (< 4 ms representative, < 8 ms stress) is the F# TacticalSceneProjection budget. This browser harness does not measure it and derives no verdict from it.
frameBudget.notABudget: frameHealth.droppedFrames is computed against a bare inline 25 ms threshold that no budget document declares. It is REPORTED as a diagnostic and is deliberately NOT gated on; see the issue filed for that discrepancy.
